doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Parker's and Eddie Jefferson's lyrics for Yardbird Suite
summary: Gates explains Parker's own lyrics 'What Price Love' and Jefferson's later lyrics.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: The lyrics, I’m familiar with “Well You Needn’t” but I didn’t know “Yardbird Suite” had lyrics.

That’s very interesting. Because Charlie Parker wrote lyrics to his own song when he was 19 years old, and the song was originally called “What Price Love.” Because he left his first wife to go make music. And he wrote the lyrics. And they’re really good lyrics too. Nobody knew that he was really a lyricist. And then later on Eddie Jefferson put lyrics to “Yardbird Suite.” So I sing ‘em both. I sing Bird’s first, the band blows, and then I go out with — and they’re both kind of historical. I mean you could tell that the first one is about love lost. “What Price Love.” And Eddie Jefferson’s is about what is the musical topic of the day/bebop so the critics say. Because he wrote ‘em in the late 50s.
